summary: Four real galaxies drawn from telescope pictures: every color is where the telescope saw it. Their thickness cannot be seen in a picture and is a guess, which the toy says and shows.

claims.claim: The colors come from ESA/Hubble's pictures of M51, M101 and M74 and ESO's picture of M83.
claims.how: tools/sp2-galaxies.mjs crops each picture round its galaxy; each splat takes the color of the pixel it is drawn from.

sources.title: Usage of ESA/Hubble Images and Videos
sources.says: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license ... provided they are clearly and visibly credited.

sources.title: The Whirlpool Galaxy (M51) and companion
sources.says: Credit: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA).

claims.claim: The thickness is a guess: a thin disk with an exponential height profile (scale height 3.5% of the radius pictured) and a round bulge.
claims.how: Each splat's height is drawn from a Laplace (two-sided exponential) distribution in the disk and from a ball in the bulge.

sources.title: Galaxy Disks
sources.publisher: P. C. van der Kruit and K. C. Freeman, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 49 (2011); arXiv:1101.1771
sources.says: Disks are mostly very flat and sometimes very thin.

claims.note: Labeled in the toy's note and About text.

simplified: The depth is guessed, not measured (said in the toy).
The disk is drawn face on as photographed; the galaxies' small tilts to us (about 20° to 30°) are not undone.
Stars of our own Galaxy in front of a galaxy, and galaxies far behind it, are drawn in its disk; M51's companion, NGC 5195, is cut off at the edge.
